title: On-call View
description: Who is being paged, how often, whether that matches the severity labels, and what the markets are doing while it happens.

panels.title: Paging now
panels.description: Alerts with page="true" in production, firing right now. Each one has a human on the hook.

panels.title: Firing, not paging
panels.description: critical and warning alerts that stay in chat.

panels.title: Active silences
panels.description: From Alertmanager itself. Every silence should carry a ticket in its comment; review weekly.

panels.title: Suppressed alerts
panels.description: Alerts hidden by a silence or an inhibition rule. What you are choosing not to see.

panels.title: Heartbeat age
panels.description: Seconds since the Watchdog alert last reached the heartbeat receiver. Above 5 minutes the alerting pipeline is broken and nothing else will page.

panels.title: Alertmanager up
panels.description: A single Alertmanager is a single point of failure. The heartbeat on the left is the external check.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: Live from the market_session_open metric (weekday sessions only, no holiday calendar). An outage during an open session is a different incident from the same outage at 3 a.m.

panels.title: Session timeline
panels.description: When each exchange was open across the dashboard range. Overlay this mentally on the paging timeline below.

panels.title: Next session event
panels.description: Time until the exchange opens (if closed) or closes (if open).

panels.title: Pages delivered per day
panels.description: Notifications the pager receiver actually got, averaged per day over the range. Green under 4 (Google SRE: two incidents per 12-hour shift).

panels.title: Page-worthy episodes per day
panels.description: Episodes of page="true" rules. The gap to the left-hand number is what grouping and inhibition saved.

targets.expr: ((sum (changes(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{page="true", environment="production"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum (min_over_time(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{page="true", environment="production"}[$__range]) > bool (time() - $__range_s)) or vector(0))) / ($__range_s / 86400)

panels.title: Severity model: critical per day
panels.description: What the pager would see if routing followed severity alone. Compare with the left: the difference is the cleanup backlog.

targets.expr: ((sum (changes(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{severity="critical", environment="production"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum (min_over_time(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{severity="critical", environment="production"}[$__range]) > bool (time() - $__range_s)) or vector(0))) / ($__range_s / 86400)

panels.title: Critical rules that do not page
panels.description: Distinct rules labelled critical in production without page="true". Each needs a decision: page, or downgrade.

targets.expr: count(count by (alertname) (count_over_time(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", severity="critical", page!="true", environment="production"}[$__range]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Pages per day
panels.description: Daily pages with the sustainable budget drawn at 4.

panels.title: Pages per hour
panels.description: Hourly resolution. Read against the session timeline above: pages outside working hours are the ones that cost sleep.

panels.title: Rules that paged
panels.description: A paging rule with many firings is paging noise: the on-call engineer sees it too often to treat it as urgent.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (alertname, owner, service) (changes(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{page="true", environment="production"}[$__range])) + sum by (alertname, owner, service) (min_over_time(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{page="true", environment="production"}[$__range]) > bool (time() - $__range_s)))

defaults.noValue: No rule paged in this range

panels.title: Severity cleanup backlog
panels.description: critical without page="true". Work through it from the top: must this wake someone at 03:00? If not, it is a warning.

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (alertname, owner) (changes(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{severity="critical", page!="true", environment="production"}[$__range])) + sum by (alertname, owner) (min_over_time(ALERTS_FOR_STATE{severity="critical", page!="true", environment="production"}[$__range]) > bool (time() - $__range_s)))

defaults.noValue: OK: every critical rule in production pages

panels.title: Paging rules outside production
panels.description: The pager route ignores these, but the label is wrong and will bite after the next routing change.

panels.title: Deliveries by receiver
panels.description: What Alertmanager delivered where. critical goes to both pager and team-chat by design; a page="true" alert missing from the pager receiver is a routing bug.
